subject: PulseHealth - Streaming chat (SSE) p99 regressions during peak / escalation
messages:
From: Marta Santiago <marta@pulsehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: James O'Leary <james.oleary@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — high p99 + connection resets during lunch peak

Hi Marissa,

We saw a sharp regression in p95/p99 for the streaming chat endpoint (SSE) today between 11:30–12:30 ET. Symptoms: increased token latency (p99 ~ 1.8s from usual ~0.4s), spikes of 503/connection reset in the client, and several streaming sessions that dropped mid-conversation. Error rate for the hour peaked at ~5%.

We attach a few artifacts: sample client-side SSE logs, server-side error traces, and a Grafana screenshot showing the p99 jump. This is impacting our clinician workflows (mid-call message drops). Can you escalate? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you'll apply credits per the SLA.

Attachments: sse-logs-pulse-20260315.zip, grafana-p99-20260315.png

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Santiago
Head of Product Ops, PulseHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Santiago <marta@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — high p99 + connection resets during lunch peak

Hi Marta — thank you for the report and artifacts. I'm very sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this immediately to our engineering and CS leads (cc'd).

Quick asks while we triage: can you confirm the exact timestamps for a few failed sessions (one sample per failure) and whether PulseHealth was sending short-lived SSE connections (sub-30s) or long-lived streams during the spike? Those details will help us determine if this is connection churn vs. inference backlog.

We're going to: 1) triage the autoscaler and request routing, 2) check our frontend proxy (NGINX) and backend error traces, and 3) push a mitigation (warm pool bump / model fallback) if needed. I'll update you within 45 minutes.

— Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:35:00Z
Subject: Investigate: PulseHealth streaming p99 spike (SSE) — urgent

Team — PulseHealth seeing p99 jump to ~1.8s + 5% 5xx between 11:30–12:30 ET. Customer impact: message drops during clinician flows. Artifacts attached by customer: sse logs + grafana shot.

Initial hypotheses:
- autoscaler didn't add warm workers fast enough under bursty short connections
- prefix/KV cache misses leading to repeated full-generation latency
- frontend (NGINX) hitting connection limits resulting in 502/connection reset

Please prioritize:
1) Check autoscaler metrics and warm-pool config for the customer's deployment and global streaming capacity (INF-4891).
2) Check proxy error logs for 502/502-related traces and connection reset patterns.
3) If autoscaler is the culprit, raise warm-pool and consider temporary model variant fallback (smaller quantized) to provide immediate latency relief.

I will tell the customer we're on it and working mitigation.

Attachments: grafana-p99-20260315.png, sse-logs-pulse-20260315.zip

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Investigate: PulseHealth streaming p99 spike (SSE) — initial triage

Quick update from infra triage:
- Autoscaler logs show sudden surge in requests at 11:28 ET with many short-lived SSE connections (median connection duration ~22s). Warm-pool was at 6 instances; scale-up lagged while new instances spun to ready state.
- NGINX at the edge reported connection resets and upstream 502s as backend queue length spiked; we also saw worker CPU on a subset of inference hosts hit ~92–95% during the peak.
- KV cache warm rate dropped during the burst (high cache miss ratio) which increased per-token latency for cold sessions.

Immediate mitigations applied at 15:55Z:
- Increased warm-pool for streaming workers to 20 instances.
- Enabled fallback policy to route new sessions to quantized model variant (compatible with PulseHealth) to reduce tail latency while we stabilize.
- Restarted a handful of over-capacity workers to reset kernel-level memory pressure (rolling restart).

Preliminary impact: p99 back down to ~0.6s in our canary tests; customer monitoring will confirm. I'm filing INF-4891 for follow-up (root cause: autoscaler warm-up + bursty short-lived connections + cache coldness). Attaching autoscaler trace.

Attachments: autoscaler-trace-20260315.txt

— Dev
Dev Patel, Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Santiago <marta@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming chat — high p99 + connection resets during lunch peak

Marta — thanks for the details. Quick update: engineering has applied an emergency mitigation (increased warm pool, enabled model fallback, rolling restarts) and we see p99 drop in our canary to ~0.6s.

Could you please keep an eye on production from your side for the next hour and send 1–2 failed session timestamps if you see anything? We'll keep monitoring and will share a full postmortem with timeline and proposed credits.

We are sorry for the impact and will propose an appropriate SLA credit once we complete the postmortem. Evelyn (CS lead) will coordinate the credit conversation and weekly follow-ups.

Best,
Marissa

Regards,
James

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z
Subject: PulseHealth incident wrap-up + next steps (postmortem + credit)

Team — final internal summary after customer sign-off:
- Incident window: 2026-03-15 11:28–15:55 ET (confirmed by customer logs). Root cause: slow autoscaler warm-up for bursty short-lived SSE connections compounded by KV cache cold-starts, leading to backend queueing and proxy 502s.
- Immediate mitigation: warm-pool bump to 20, model fallback to quantized variant, rolling restart. Impact: p99 reduced to acceptable range; customer verified improvement.
- Customer requested credit: propose 20% credit for March invoice (per previous SLA precedents). Evelyn — please prepare the credit offer and legal sign-off.

Action items assigned:
- INF-4891: Autoscaler warm-up tuning and warm-pool auto-scaling rules for streaming (Dev + Logan) — owner: dev_patel — ETA: 2 weeks.
- INF-4900: Add SSE p99 alerting + runbook and a streaming-specific connection churn metric (Platform) — owner: logan_wright — ETA: 1 week.
- CS: coordinate weekly stability sync with PulseHealth for 2 weeks — owner: evelyn_hart.

Postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/pulsehealth-2026-03-15
JIRA: INF-4891, INF-4900

I'll coordinate exec approval for the credit path this morning (looping in Finance). Good job triaging quickly.

— Marissa
